title: Car spaces could be sold separately from apartments so that only buyers who want parking pay for it
oneLiner: Grattan's companion proposal: unbundle the space from the home.
body: Alongside removing minimums, Grattan recommends removing parking maximums and allowing car spaces to be titled and sold separately from dwellings, so a household without a car is not obliged to buy one and a household with two can buy two.
contextBackground: Unbundling turns parking from a planning quantity into a priced good, which is the logic of the whole proposal carried to the sale contract.
contextDisagreement: Strata and lending rules complicate separate titling; opponents also note it does nothing for street parking.

evidenceItems.citation: Grattan Institute, Wasted space, May 2026 — recommendations

otherClaim.title: Councils should abolish minimum parking requirements for new housing

claimItself.title: Councils should abolish minimum parking requirements for new housing
claimItself.oneLiner: Whether planning schemes should stop requiring a set number of car spaces per new dwelling and let builders decide.
claimItself.body: Most Australian planning schemes require new apartments and townhouses to include a minimum number of off-street car spaces, typically one or more per dwelling. The proposal removes the minimum. Developers could still build parking; they would no longer be required to.

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: Parking minimums add roughly $70,000 to the cost of a two-bedroom apartment in Sydney, $62,000 in Melbourne and up to $137,000 in Perth

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: Auckland removed minimum parking requirements citywide in 2016, and new developments near frequent transit have since provided markedly less parking

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: New housing completions have not kept pace with population growth in Australia's largest cities over the past decade

usedIn.relationSentence: This claim supports “Councils should abolish minimum parking requirements for new housing”

strengthDefinitions.decisive: The parent claim largely stands or falls on this one.
strengthDefinitions.relevant: It adds real weight, but the parent claim survives without it.
strengthDefinitions.tangential: True perhaps, but it does little work for this claim.
